name: Autosomal Dominant Intermediate Charcot-Marie-Tooth Disease Type C

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: Clinical and Electrophysiological Diagnostic Criteria for CMT

criteria.description: Progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy predominantly affecting lower limbs
Intermediate motor nerve conduction velocities (25-45 m/s) on electrophysiological studies
Identification of pathogenic mutation in relevant genes associated with CMT type C (e.g., DNM2 gene)
Autosomal dominant inheritance pattern with affected first-degree relatives
Presence of pes cavus and sensory loss in distal extremities

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: Presence of progressive distal muscle weakness and atrophy with intermediate nerve conduction velocities plus genetic confirmation or compatible family history
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Electrophysiological studies are critical to distinguish intermediate CMT from demyelinating or axonal subtypes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Distal muscle weakness and atrophy of lower limbs
Intermediate motor nerve conduction velocity slowing (25-45 m/s)
searchTerms: moderate slowing of motor nerve signals

common.symptomName: Distal sensory loss in lower limbs
searchTerms: loss of feeling in lower feet and legs
reduced sensation in feet and legs

common.symptomName: Steppage gait due to foot drop
searchTerms: steppage gait due to foot drop

common.symptomName: Reduced or absent deep tendon reflexes

occasional.symptomName: Mild distal sensory neuropathy in upper limbs
searchTerms: early sensory loss in upper limbs
slight sensory nerve damage in arms

occasional.symptomName: Foot deformities other than pes cavus (e.g., hammer toes)
searchTerms: toe shape abnormalities other than high arches
claw toes and similar foot issues
mild problems with automatic body functions

laboratory: Nerve biopsy may show intermediate features between demyelination and axonal loss
imaging: MRI may show muscle atrophy in distal limbs
Nerve ultrasound may reveal nerve enlargement
other: Electrophysiological studies demonstrating intermediate nerve conduction velocities

distinguishingFeatures: Markedly slowed nerve conduction velocities (< 38 m/s)
Normal or mildly reduced nerve conduction velocities (> 45 m/s)

redFlags: Rapidly progressive weakness or sensory loss
references: Pareyson D, Marchesi C. Diagnosis, natural history, and management of Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Lancet Neurol. 2009;8(7):654-667.
Rossor AM, Polke JM, Houlden H, Reilly MM. Clinical implications of genetic advances in Charcot-Marie-Tooth disease. Nat Rev Neurol. 2013;9(10):562-571.
